newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, market seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, market seen stable.

text.p: Croatian stocks opened the week's trading mixed on Tuesday with mild losses among leading hotels, but traders predicted overall stability would reign for some time.
"Market may have been slightly overheated last week and this is only a slight cooling down," Dubravko Zganec, head of trading at FIMA brokerage, told Reuters.
"Prices will remain more or less stable, with slight fluctuations," he added.
Seven of 14 actively traded stocks rose, six fell and one was flat in thin Tuesday trade. Turnover fell to 8.3 million kuna on volume of 10,143 shares.
Most actively traded stock was fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka, which added 54 kuna to 1,890, selling 2,799 shares.
Zagrebacka's E-series preferred stock slid 30 kuna to 1,070 with 593 shares sold. Its bearer C-series surged 100 kuna to 900 but only two shares changed hands.
Another blue chip, drugs firm Pliva, rose five kuna to 475 on volume of 1,265 units.
Four of seven hoteliers were among decliners, led by Riviera, losing 7.3 percent to 204 kuna and selling 410 shares.
Zlatni Rat from the central Dalmatian island of Brac was the biggest gainer, doubling its value to 220 kuna, though on a small volume of 10 shares. It last traded in October 1996.
Suncani Hvar, the most active among hoteliers, gained two kuna to 70 with 2,217 units changing hands.
Arenaturist slid 6.1 percent to 180 kuna on volume of 150. Jadranturist fell 4.8 percent to 315 kuna and sold 310 units and Istraturist lost two percent to end at 245 kuna.
Food giant Podravka fell 15 kuna or 4.3 percent to 335 kuna. Investor interest seemed to weaken to produce a volume of 1,362 -- much lower than lately.
Chocolate maker Kras gained five kuna to 460 on volume of 436 and Adriatic pipeline operator Janaf was flat at 9,000, trading 19 units.
